historical_validation: cpu-check-01 failed because the staging constant was GPU-feature-gated. Preserved and excluded from fresh success counts; final -02 matrix uses the common host-memory constant.
inherited_observer_validation: 17 tests from 9.154; source unchanged, excluded from fresh counts
limitations: The combined ceiling covers requests delegated by SpillAlloc to System and full backing of SpillAlloc mappings, including headers/rounding and in-flight reservations. Allocator metadata/retention, foreign allocations, other direct mappings, file-cache/kernel storage and complete RSS remain outside this request ledger.
Mapped GPU staging keeps a separate 64 MiB reservation from the engine source bound. Mapping pathname/size observations do not authenticate driver ownership or establish driver pinning bounds.

Conservatively charging nonresident disk-backed spill can reject a larger out-of-core workload that previously relied on reclaim. Infallible allocation failure can abort a worker; reservations stay held through physical worker exit.

The optional spill-to-System fallback exists only without a configured spill cap. A configured spill failure still rejects. Failed unmapping retains reservations and invalidates accounting rather than authorizing new ownership.
Worker startup installs the combined limit before Rayon/GPU and cannot relax it. Other entry points without worker admission do not gain an active limit.

The pressure fixture deliberately retains foreign C allocations, which are outside Rust request accounting. The private-data cap and allocator reuse/retirement checks remain separate and do not constitute full lifetime admission.

Ordinary incomplete workload profiles still reject. All maintained proving routes, broader/live-cache workloads, five matched throughput pairs, 24 hours AND 150 roots, full-64/deadline/depth/size gates, multiple GPUs, AMD/Metal and pending Apple source integration remain open.
